newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS BREEZES PAST GIMELSTOB IN RETURN TO ACTION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS BREEZES PAST GIMELSTOB IN RETURN TO ACTION.

text.p: Playing his first match since winning a fourth Wimbledon title last month, Pete Sampras posted a quick and painless 6-2 6-4 second-round victory over fellow American Justin Gimelstob Wednesday night at the ATP Championship.
Sampras, who has won 10 Grand Slam trophies and 48 career titles, was pleased to find that taking a month off since Wimbledon has not affected his game.

"I was a little surprised," Sampras said after the 73-minute match. "As much as you can practice, it's always different in a match situation. I saw the ball really well. If I'm playing well, I'm pretty tough to beat."
For the 88th-ranked Gimelstob, a frequent practice partner of Sampras's, losing to the world number one is far from a miserable experience in his first full year on the tour.
"If he maximizes his game and he's playing up to his potential, I'd like to see him play God," Gimelstob said. "If I'm going to lose it might as well be to the best player ever."
Second seed Michael Chang came back from losing a first-set tiebreaker to win a second-round match 6-7 (4-7) 6-1 6-2 over Wayne Ferreira of South Africa in one hour, 51 minutes.

Other marquee names moving into the third round were third seed Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia, fifth seed Thomas Muster of Austria, sixth seed Sergi Bruguera of Spain, seventh seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia, ninth seed Marcelo Rios of Chile, 10th seed Gustavo Kuerten of Brazil, 14th seed Albert Costa of Spain and 16th seed Patrick Rafter of Australia.
American Chris Woodruff, last week's big surprise story on the men's tour, was a second-round 7-6 (7-3) 7-6 (8-6) loser to the sixth-ranked Kafelnikov.

Woodruff's ranking moved from 57th to 30th in the world following his first career tournament victory at Montreal last Sunday -- a win that included victories over Ivanisevic, Mark Philippoussis, Kafelnikov and Kuerten, four players all ranked amongst the top 15 in the world.
Sampras posted a 68 percent first-serve efficiency and floated around the court all night, hitting stinging serves, adept volleys and winner groundstrokes.
"For me, it's about being mentally fresh," Sampras said. "I need to stay fresh and feel eager."

Gimelstob had two chances to challenge Sampras on his serve all night and both came too late in the match. With Sampras ahead 6-2 4-3, Gimelstob had two break point opportunities at 15-40 in the eighth game. Sampras saved both with superbly placed aces.
Chang, ranked second in the world, fell behind 6-1 in the first-set tiebreaker before winning the next three points. But the 27th-ranked Ferreira won the next point with an ace to take the set.

"I was hoping that I would be able to kind of sink my way back in there," Chang said of the tiebreaker. "You never know when you are able to turn things around and sometimes you are, and sometimes you aren't."
From that point on, the match was safely in Chang's control.
